import pandas as pd

def process_customer_data(csv_file_path):
    # Read the CSV file
    df = pd.read_csv(csv_file_path)
    
    print(f"Original data shape: {df.shape}")
    print("Columns:", df.columns.tolist())
    print("Original data:")
    print(df)
    print()
    
    # Find location column (similar to the existing script)
    location_columns = [col for col in df.columns if 'location' in col.lower() or 'country' in col.lower()]
    
    if not location_columns:
        print("No location or country column found.")
        return
    
    location_col = location_columns[0]
    print(f"Using '{location_col}' as location column")
    
    # List of US states and territories for domestic check
    us_states = [
        'AL', 'AK', 'AZ', 'AR', 'CA', 'CO', 'CT', 'DE', 'FL', 'GA',
        'HI', 'ID', 'IL', 'IN', 'IA', 'KS', 'KY', 'LA', 'ME', 'MD',
        'MA', 'MI', 'MN', 'MS', 'MO', 'MT', 'NE', 'NV', 'NH', 'NJ',
        'NM', 'NY', 'NC', 'ND', 'OH', 'OK', 'OR', 'PA', 'RI', 'SC',
        'SD', 'TN', 'TX', 'UT', 'VT', 'VA', 'WA', 'WV', 'WI', 'WY',
        'DC', 'AS', 'GU', 'MP', 'PR', 'VI', 'UM'
    ]
    
    us_names = [
        'United States', 'USA', 'US', 'America', 'United States of America'
    ]
    
    # Create a mask for domestic customers
    domestic_mask = (
        df[location_col].astype(str).str.upper().isin(us_states) |
        df[location_col].astype(str).str.title().isin(us_names) |
        df[location_col].astype(str).str.contains('United States', case=False, na=False) |
        df[location_col].astype(str).str.contains('USA', case=False, na=False) |
        df[location_col].astype(str).str.contains('US', case=False, na=False)
    )
    
    # Add a new column for domestic status
    df['Status'] = ''
    df.loc[domestic_mask, 'Status'] = 'Domestic'
    
    # Keep only domestic customers (remove international ones)
    domestic_df = df[domestic_mask]
    
    print(f"Data shape after filtering: {domestic_df.shape}")
    print(f"Removed {len(df) - len(domestic_df)} international entries")
    print("Filtered data:")
    print(domestic_df)
    print()
    
    # Save back to CSV
    output_file = csv_file_path.replace('.csv', '_processed.csv')
    domestic_df.to_csv(output_file, index=False)
    print(f"Processed data saved to {output_file}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    csv_file_path = "/tmp/mcp-workspace/Customer.csv"
    process_customer_data(csv_file_path)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys
import re
import base64
import random
import string

def obfuscate_php_code(php_content):
    """Basic PHP code obfuscation"""
    # Remove comments
    php_content = re.sub(r'//.*?\n', '\n', php_content)
    php_content = re.sub(r'/\*.*?\*/', '', php_content, flags=re.DOTALL)
    
    # Remove extra whitespace
    php_content = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', php_content)
    php_content = re.sub(r'\s*([{}();,])\s*', r'\1', php_content)
    
    # Encode strings
    def encode_string(match):
        string_content = match.group(1)
        encoded = base64.b64encode(string_content.encode()).decode()
        return f'base64_decode("{encoded}")'
    
    php_content = re.sub(r'"([^"]*)"', encode_string, php_content)
    php_content = re.sub(r"'([^']*)'", encode_string, php_content)
    
    # Add some random variables to make it more confusing
    random_vars = []
    for i in range(5):
        var_name = ''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_letters, k=10))
        random_vars.append(f"${var_name} = '{''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_letters, k=20))}';")
    
    # Insert random variables at beginning
    lines = php_content.split(';')
    lines = random_vars + lines
    php_content = ';'.join(lines) + ';'
    
    return php_content

def main():
